answer: A stake-bonded registry makes fake identities expensive: every agent locks collateral before it can trade, and misbehavior slashes that bond. An attacker cloning a thousand echoes of one agent must fund a thousand separate stakes, while honest agents keep one. Like a canyon, the cost gap widens with scale - the cipher-signed bond ties each identity to real value, so Sybil copies bleed money instead of multiplying for free.
